status: Mordecai 0.4 production baseline · eight decks · content/balance audit pending

decks.name: Bad Decisions — Reckless Audit
watchpoints: Does combat reliably unlock Trouble and draw?
Are repeated Attacks and dice choices fun?
Which singletons deserve more copies after this coverage test?
decks.status_note: 32 locked Reckless cards, all represented in this 40-card coverage deck. Eight extra copies support early bodies, Victory Lap and Did You See That?!. Deliberately broad for card verification, not a tuned competitive list. Last slot in 33-card Style target remains open.
decks.passive: Whenever one of your Characters Defeats an opposing Character with an Attack, the opposing Leader loses 1 Composure.
decks.breaking_point: You Ain’t Seen Nothing Yet! Roll a D6: 1 — Rotate a chosen Ready friendly Character; 2–5 — Ready a chosen friendly Rotated Character; 6 — Ready all your Characters.

decks.name: Comeback Tour
mulligan_priority: Reply All, Reset the Vibes, or another refill bridge
watchpoints: Can the deck intentionally reach zero cards without making obviously bad plays?
Does Comeback Tour refill often enough to sustain Momentum without causing routine deck-out?
Do acceleration cards help create explosive turns rather than simply emptying the hand?
decks.status_note: Landon Rock Star lab promoted to Mordecai as a TESTING translation. Bad Publicity Is Still Publicity: whenever this Leader loses Composure, Draw that many cards. The 40-card Comeback Tour list is unchanged; balance evidence is pending under Mordecai.

decks.name: Now You See Me
mulligan_priority: Trap Door and a Dismiss enabler
A return effect and a payoff
watchpoints: Rabbit / Dove / Now You See Me / Now You Don’t / Trap Door resource costs and optional choices
Headliner’s 5 Trouble payoff requires live board presence and a return each turn
Marked Deck and Encore draw efficiency; short decks and Last Straw sequencing
Party Mom combat and return tempo; borrowed ownership and entrance effects
decks.status_note: 8 October locked audit implemented. Coverage baseline: all 32 designs, 26 Characters / 10 Actions / 4 Items. Copy distribution is a testing baseline, not a balance claim.
decks.passive: The Show Must Go On: Once during your turn, when a character you control is returned to your hand or Dismissed, Ready 1 Stash.
decks.breaking_point: For My Next Trick…: You may return a character you control to your hand. Then you may play a character costing 3 or less from your hand without paying its cost.

decks.name: Curbside Empire
watchpoints: Is Jerry-Rig useful without becoming free permanent ramp?
Does Trash Baron create enough incentive to leave opposing Stash unspent?
Can Salvage reach Big Hand through scavenging rather than generic Draw?
decks.status_note: Revision 12 baseline; one Good as New added as Salvage Return counterplay.

decks.name: Neighborhood Watch — Stonewall Audit
watchpoints: Does Round 8 create a satisfying payoff?
Can opponents break Meat Shield, Absorb and healing boards?
Are Lawyer stacks and repeatable Ready effects fair?
decks.status_note: 33-card Stonewall audit; 40-card baseline includes every locked card. Count reconciliation: one card over the intended 32; no locked card removed. Balance provisional.
decks.passive: Failure to Respond: Beginning in Round 8, your Characters get +1 Trouble.
decks.breaking_point: Final Warning: When an opposing Character Causes Trouble that triggers your Breaking Point, you may Dismiss that Character after its Trouble resolves.

decks.name: Tag Team Trashfire
mulligan_priority: A cheap Wrestler or sacrifice body
Tag Me In! or a sacrifice payoff
watchpoints: How often does Stash-scaled Tag Out put a Character directly into play versus put the revealed card into hand?
Does Tag Out create exciting Hothead replacement attacks without excessive free-board snowballing?
Does recursion feel distinct from Salvage and self-damage distinct from Reckless?
decks.status_note: Revision 12 baseline; Stash-scaled Tag Out is the active Leader passive.

decks.name: Strength in Numbers............ Mostly Numbers........ Probably.
mulligan_priority: Shoebox of Dead Cats when the rest of the hand can establish Cats
Shovel when a Shoebox plan is already developing
Hairy Cat when the opposing deck relies on multiple small attackers
Avoid keeping Nine Lives, Zero Survivors in an otherwise slow opening hand
Avoid keeping Mittens III unless the rest of the hand can establish the colony or Shoebox plan
watchpoints: How often the below-3-Cats mode allows a second Stash
Whether spending two cards on Stash helps rebuild or leaves the Cat player too low on hand size
How often the 3-or-more-Cats mode draws the additional card
Whether the extra Draw actually lets the Cat player sustain a second wave after trading Characters
Whether switching between the two passive modes feels like Momentum rather than a punishment for losing Cats
How often Shoebox reaches three buried Cats
Whether the +1 Power threshold makes Shoebox worthwhile even without drawing Shovel
Whether four Shovels make random resurrection too consistent
How often Shovel hits a cheap Cat versus a high-cost Cat
Whether Nine Lives, Zero Survivors is a meaningful comeback instead of an automatic reset button
Whether refilling both players to seven over-rewards the player who casts the wipe
Whether Snowball creates meaningful protect-or-risk decisions
Whether Hairy Cat creates interesting attack sequencing or simply discourages combat
Whether four Mittens III copies make the engine too central to the deck
Whether Mittens III creates a real attack-versus-feed decision instead of always eating Stash
How often Mittens III cashes in Shoebox Cats, and whether that payoff is exciting without making Shoebox automatic fuel
decks.status_note: Landon Lab 1.3 / STANK-66 Cat Lady promoted to Mordecai. Strength in Numbers split passive: below 3 Cats, may Stash twice that Turn; at 3+ Cats, Draw one additional card at start of Turn. Shoebox/Shovel, Snowball, Hairy Cat, Three-Legged Cat, and Mittens III behaviors are production playtest mechanics.
decks.deckbuilding_exception: May include Cat Characters from any Style and up to 10 copies of Stray Cat.

decks.name: Fully Charged, No Charger
mulligan_priority: It's Alive! plus at least two Characters
Lab Assistant if It's Alive! is missing
Avoid hands with too many recharge cards before spending the initial battery
watchpoints: How much of the five-charge battery is spent on Turn 1
Whether holding charge for a later Turn is better than emptying the battery
Abominations created by Round
Power/Health roll distributions and how much each stat affects outcomes
Whether low-roll Abominations create funny setbacks without making games feel decided by one die
Whether high-roll Abominations feel like jackpots without creating non-games
Turns where the Scientist has cards to play but insufficient Ready Stash
How often Flip the Breaker and Car Battery in the Bathtub extend the battery meaningfully
Whether the opponent can survive an explosive opening and capitalize on Burnout
Whether Specimens are fun physical theater without becoming rules overhead
decks.status_note: STANK INDUSTRIES-60 Mad Scientist rulebreaker deck merged into Composure. Abominations have fixed 2 Trouble in this first compatibility pass; Specimens have 1.
